historical_growth.growth_rate_source: forward: management FY26-FY30 revenue CAGR target 4-5% (Aug-26 FY30 targets) haircut to a ~2.7% CAGR base path over FY26-FY35 on statutory revenue; no historical CAGR is usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All historical CAGRs describe the FY21-FY26 divestment/portfolio-exit programme (disposal proceeds $395.9m FY21, $245.4m FY22, $160.5m FY23, $68.5m FY24, $61.9m FY25, $76.9m H1 FY26) and the FY23 impairment year, not the continuing business. Equity CAGR (-7.5% 3yr) is dominated by the $539.5m FY23 impairment and by dividends+buybacks exceeding statutory earnings; FCF CAGRs are off trough bases (owner FCF FY22 $45m, FY20/FY23 negative) and are meaningless. EPS 5yr CAGR is null because FY20 EPS was negative (-$0.266).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF (treatment B) series: FY20 -337.3, FY21 231.8, FY22 45.4, FY23 -116.8, FY24 219.5, FY25 271.1 vs reported FCF -173.6, 430.1, 215.6, 55.2, 397.8, 439.6. Lease principal ($148-195m/yr) is the entire gap; SBC ($3-5m) is immaterial. Reported FCF 3yr CAGR 26.8% vs owner 81.5% is base-effect noise, not SBC growth.

scenario_narratives.base: Downer is a low-margin, government-facing infrastructure services contractor whose value rests on two axes: whether the post-FY23 risk guardrails hold (no repeat of the mispriced-contract blow-up that produced the $539.5m impairment) and whether the margin-led recovery (EBITA 2.6% FY23 -> 4.4% FY25 -> 5.1% FY26) can continue on a top line that has shrunk three years running through deliberate exits. Base: statutory revenue troughs in FY26 (-6%), is flat in FY27 as exits annualise and the guided soft 1H27 plays out, then grows 3-3.5% off the record $38.5bn work-in-hand; EBITA reaches ~5.5% underlying by FY29 (short of the ~6% FY30 aspiration) and recurring restructuring/legal cash costs fade to ~0.2% of revenue. Leases (~1.5% of revenue) and ROADS hybrids are charged once. Owner FCF rises from ~$270m (FY25, tax-light) to ~$370-400m as the cash tax rate normalises to 30% and capex reverts toward depreciation.
scenario_narratives.bull: The FY30 targets land as stated: 4-5% revenue CAGR from FY27 as energy-transition (transmission, Powerco, Chorus, AusNet), defence estate and QTMP/CRL programs convert the order book, EBITA approaching 6% by FY30 on continued cost-out and disciplined tendering, ISIs fade to a residual 0.1pp, and cash conversion stays >90% funding the ~$260m buyback and 60-70% NPATA payout. Terminal growth 3.0%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The turnaround proves margin-limited and reputationally fragile: a fixed-price contract miss or persistent defence/QTMP ramp costs hold EBITA at ~4.3-4.5%, the shareholder class action and ACCC cartel proceedings against Spotless settle for cash and dent government re-tender win rates, pro forma revenue keeps contracting through FY28 and thereafter grows only 2%, and capex has to catch up with a rationalised fleet. Owner FCF stays near the FY25 level in real terms. Terminal growth 2.0%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Downer as a mid-cycle stream of unlevered owner FCF built from components (underlying EBITDA less a recurring-ISI haircut, less lease cash, D&A ex-ROU, a normalised 30% cash tax and capex reverting toward depreciation) rather than off FY25's tax-light reported FCF or a single peak-margin year. Growth is anchored to guidance and work-in-hand, not to historical CAGRs that describe the divestment programme. Risk is charged in the flows and the scenario weights at a single 9% AUD WACC, with a 15x FCF cap on the terminal value for a thin-margin contractor.
key_risks_to_valuation: Contract mispricing / execution: a single large fixed-price loss can erase a year of margin gains (FY23 precedent)
Legal overhangs: consolidated shareholder class action (Vic SC) and ACCC cartel proceedings against Spotless; unquantified, handled in the bear flows and weights rather than a bridge deduction
Revenue base: pro forma revenue down three consecutive years; the FY30 4-5% CAGR target is not yet evidenced
Near-term: guided 1H27 revenue/earnings/margin below pcp (defence P&AS ramp-up, QTMP transition); shares fell ~12% on the FY26 result
Data vintage: FY26 annual report not yet in corpus; balance sheet and share count are Dec-2025
Terminal value: ~60-70% of EV at a 9% WACC; 15x cap binds in the bull case

inputs.share_count_basis: 663.14m ordinary shares on issue at 31 Dec 2025 (H1 FY26 note D3, after 8.4m bought back) plus ~3.7m dilutive executive incentive shares (diluted WANOS 671.9 vs basic 668.2, note B6). The $230m/$260m buyback continued in H2 FY26 (~$96.5m cumulative by 30 Jun 2026 per FY26 result) so today's count is ~4-5m lower; refresh from the FY26 annual report.
inputs.sbc_source: Group share-based employee benefits expense, FY2025 Annual Report (financial-parser series: FY18 2.8, FY19 4.0, FY20 4.8, FY21 -0.4, FY22 4.2, FY23 -0.8, FY24 3.2, FY25 3.7); equity-award cash taxes nil (KPI EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every year). SBC-near-zero market.
inputs.buyback_note: FY25 nil; H1 FY26 $64.4m on-market (H1 FY26 cash flow statement line 1297). $230m program approved 21 Aug 2025; Analysis JSON reports ~$96.5m repurchased by 30 Jun 2026 with continuation into FY27.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company definition (H1 FY26 report p.15): borrowings excluding lease liabilities, at face value including deferred finance costs and derivative MTM, less cash = $242.3m at 31 Dec 2025 (Jun-25: $259.3m). Balance-sheet carrying values: borrowings 501.1 current + 394.3 non-current = 895.4; cash 683.4; total_debt here = 683.4 + 242.3 = 925.7 (face value). Lease liabilities 100.4 + 299.7 = 400.1 are EXCLUDED because the lease cash cost is charged inside the flows (treatment B). The Metrics.csv total_debt of 1,295.5 includes those leases and must not be combined with these flows.
inputs.owner_fcf_definition: last_fcf = reported_fcf (OCF 562.5 - gross capex 122.9 = 439.6) - SBC 3.7 - interest income 17.2 - lease principal 147.6 = 271.1. Lease interest (26.9) is already inside OCF. Interest income is stripped because the $683m gross cash is netted in the bridge (section 7d: asset in the bridge, its income out of the flows). Company's own 'free cash flow' is $323.9m (OCF - net capex - lease principal +/- JV advances).

owner_fcf_history.note: Treatment-B owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - interest income - lease principal (lease principal: FY20 152.9, FY21 194.5, FY22 163.6, FY23 165.0, FY24 163.5, FY25 147.6, H1 FY26 63.0)

inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD flows discounted at an AUD-built WACC: risk-free ~4.4% (ACGB 10y, Sep-26), ERP 5.5%, beta ~1.05 for an ASX contractor -> cost of equity ~10.2%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.5% (BBB, Fitch reaffirmed Feb-26) -> 3.9% after 30% tax; D/(D+E) ~17% at market (net debt+ROADS ~$0.4bn vs ~$4.4bn market cap, gross debt ~$0.9bn) -> WACC ~9.0%. One WACC across all three scenarios; cyclicality, contract-loss and legal risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: B - leases as operating cost. lease_cost_pct_path charges principal + interest (FY25: 147.6 + 26.9 = 174.5 = 1.66% of revenue; H1 FY26: 63.0 + 11.6 = 74.6 = 1.55%) inside EBIT; lease liabilities ($400.1m at Dec-25) are excluded from net debt; da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (FY25: 201.6 'other non-current assets' = 1.92% of revenue, vs 140.9 ROU depreciation; FY24: 192.7 vs 153.3), so the lease is charged once and cash-tax EBIT is not double-hit.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: 200m NZ$1 ROADS preference shares in Works Finance (NZ) Ltd, classified as equity NCI (book $178.6m; $172.7m at Dec-25 spot per note B6(iii)). Their 7.27% gross / 5.23% cash distribution is a financing flow outside unlevered owner FCF, so the instrument is deducted at $172.7m in equity_bridge and its conversion shares are NOT added to the count (anti-dilutive at Dec-25). Equity-accounted JV income is inside EBITDA/OCF (distributions in OCF), so JV stakes are not added to the bridge.
inputs.ebitda_basis: ebitda_margin_path is post-IFRS-16 (pre-lease) EBITDA on statutory revenue, on an UNDERLYING basis less a haircut for recurring 'individually significant items' cash costs. Reference points: FY25 underlying EBITA 474.2 (4.52%) + D&A ex acquired-intangible amortisation 321.5 = 795.7 = 7.59%; statutory EBITDA 625.7 = 5.97% after $163.5m ISIs (FY24 ISIs 177.2; FY26 ~95 pre-tax; H1 FY26 42.2). FY26 actual underlying EBITA 502.9 = 5.1% (Aug-26 result, from Analysis JSON) implies underlying EBITDA ~8.1%. Base haircuts 0.4pp in FY26-27 fading to 0.2pp, since exits/restructuring/legal costs have recurred every year since FY20.

bear.rationale: The margin recovery stalls at FY25-26 levels and partially reverses: a contract-pricing miss or the 1H27 defence/QTMP ramp costs persist (EBITA ~4.3-4.5%), ISIs keep recurring at ~0.5pp (class-action settlement, ACCC penalty, further exit costs), pro forma revenue keeps shrinking through FY28 and never recovers beyond 2%, and fleet renewal capex catches up with depreciation.

base.growth_rationale: FY26 -6.0%: H1 FY26 statutory revenue -7.1% (4,828 vs 5,196) on E&U contract exits, NZ Cleaning and Keolis Downer disposals; FY26 EBITA 502.9 at 5.1% implies ~$9.85bn. FY27 +1.0%: exits annualise, management guides 1H27 revenue below pcp with a 2H27 recovery. FY28-30 3.0-3.5%: work-in-hand $35.1bn -> $38.5bn (+10%) and the FY30 4-5% CAGR target, haircut because pro forma revenue has fallen three years running. Fade to 2.5% nominal.
base.margin_rationale: Underlying EBITDA 7.6% FY25 -> ~8.1% FY26 (EBITA 4.4% -> 5.1%); base carries EBITA to ~5.5% underlying by FY29 (management: 'approaching 6%' by FY30) less a recurring-ISI haircut of 0.4pp fading to 0.2pp -> 7.7% rising to 8.2% post-IFRS-16 EBITDA. FY27 held flat for the guided 1H27 defence ramp-up and QTMP transition costs.
base.capex_da_rationale: Gross capex 1.17% FY25 / 1.33% FY24 is below the 2.3-2.5% of FY21-23 after fleet rationalisation; base lifts it to 1.5%, converging on D&A ex-ROU ex-acquired-intangible amortisation (~1.5-1.6%). da_pct is D&A ex-ROU (1.92% FY25, 1.75% FY24, ~1.65% H1 FY26 run-rate) drifting to 1.7% as acquired-intangible amortisation (~0.2%) runs off.
base.tax_rationale: H1 FY26 cash tax 53.9 on ~184 underlying PBT = 29%; FY24-25 cash tax (10.6, 45.5) was depressed by loss utilisation and ISI deductions and is not repeatable. Statutory 30% AU / 28% NZ.
base.wc_rationale: Contractor with receivables/contract assets against payables and $220-250m deferred revenue; cash conversion 86-98% of EBITDA. Growth consumes ~5c per $ of incremental revenue; the FY26 revenue decline releases a little.

bull.rationale: Management's FY30 targets delivered in full: 4-5% revenue CAGR from FY27 on the $38.5bn order book and energy-transition/defence tailwinds, EBITA margin reaching ~6% by FY30 (underlying EBITDA ~9.0%) with ISIs fading to ~0.1pp as the portfolio reset completes.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the FY23 mispricing crisis is recent, the risk guardrails are unproven through a full cycle, two legal overhangs (class action, ACCC cartel proceedings) are unresolved, ISIs have recurred every year since FY20, and management has already guided a soft 1H27. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs revenue growth to reverse a three-year decline AND margins to reach ~6% simultaneously. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
